findings: README, shell launcher and both entrypoint classes fully read. Project replicates StackOverflow duplicate-question retrieval/classification experiments using preprocessed posts/tags/code and PostgreSQL; not file/image identity. README describes recall@k for BM25/DupPredictor/Stanford/cosine/Weka. Results/papers/dumps were not independently verified or fetched.

Spring PostConstruct runs bucket generation and optional feature generation/classification, truncates local dupe.log and calls cleanOldData. No runtime executed, database contacted or dump installed. Shell launcher requests70GiB max heap; README experiment hardware80GBRAM and restore100GB are upstream claims only. Root MIT metadata differs Apache notice in DupeApplication; no code adopted.85blob inventory includes many committed class files, not85independent source modules.

CosineSimilarity and SimpleLogisticClassifier fully read. Three cosine APIs have inconsistent empty-vector behavior: numeric arrays explicitly return0 for zero norm, space-token string scorer divides0/0 for empty text, regex-token string scorer does not guard zero norm and can count empty tokens. String bag scorer repeatedly indexes LinkedList, introducing quadratic traversal over vocabulary; regex dot product multiplies Integer counts before widening, allowing int overflow on high counts. No finite-value validation.

Logistic regression uses fixed3000passes,rate0.0001,no bias unless supplied as feature,no regularization/shuffle/convergence gate and unchecked feature lengths/labels. Dataset reader parses integer columns, skips first and uses last as label, with no blank-line/schema validation. Sigmoid likelihood calculations can hit log0/NaN and likelihood is unused. No calibration or original-file identity proof. Source review only, no Java/dependency runtime execution.

FeaturesService and generic repository interface/implementation fully read. Positive pairs derive duplicate postlinks, require master answers/existence/common-tag substring; negatives are randomly sampled open questions paired with shuffled duplicate questions. Open question status is not independent proof of semantic nonduplication. Random SQL/shuffle has no fixed seed and negative sample has no same maxCreationDate cutoff, limiting reproducibility and temporal equivalence.

Positive generation saves pair then features, catches exceptions and System.exit1; negative generation catches errors and continues after potential pair save, without explicit incomplete receipt. Class-level transaction annotation alone does not prove rollback after swallowed exceptions. cleanOldData deletes old feature/pair rows for tag; no database actions executed.

Repository blank-title/body branches continue normalization loop without removing those posts from returned list. fetchPairs optional limit lacks order; tag/date values concatenated into SQL rather than all bound parameters. Per-positive master answer count and post fetch imply repeated database queries. These source-derived dataset/operational limitations prevent treating recall@k claims as generic file-dedup coverage; classifier evaluation remains unread.

Lucene BM25 and Terrier PL2 search services fully read. Both concatenate title/body/tag synonyms and index in RAM, retain mutable last search results and return bounded candidates, not exhaustive duplicate pairs. Lucene indexes StandardAnalyzer but queries WhitespaceAnalyzer despite same-analyzer comment; token normalization mismatch can affect recall. No independent candidate completeness oracle or memory/cancellation budget.

Lucene parse retry doubles global BooleanQuery clause cap without bounded retry/resource ceiling; exception cause dereferenced without null guard. Escape operation mutates query string on each retry, potentially repeated escaping. Reader close is finalize-named method, not explicit scoped lifetime; index/analyzers not closed here. Rebuild does not visibly clear question cache or reset index, so repeated use contract remains unqualified.

Terrier sets global application properties, English tokenizes and parses unescaped query content, exits JVM on index construction failure, and exposes result index lookup without explicit range/state checks. PL2 maxResultSize limits candidate retrieval. No search runtime/dependency tests were executed; useful retrieval-ranking concepts do not establish exact original-file equality.

DupeUtils fully read. Main feature path calculateCosine guards null/trim-empty and returns0 before calling space-token cosine, mitigating raw empty-string NaN in this caller. Seven ordered field/crossfield cosine features are extracted. Missing values and true dissimilarity both become0, with no separate missingness signal; this is a model choice, not proof of equality.

createFeatures explicitly orders seven feature names. Alternative createFeaturesForSimpleClassifier allocates five doubles but iterates all features except EE/AA, which are not among current seven; current schema can exceed array bounds and HashMap iteration lacks canonical ordering. Caller reachability not yet verified. Stanford Dataset consumes double values as categorical features rather than explicit named numeric counters in this helper; calibration not established.

generateBuckets builds master-to-direct-duplicates sets, not transitive closure. allDuplicatedQuestionsIds adds postLink.getId instead of getPostId; use/reachability unverified. Global static cached postlinks/buckets are not invalidated when setAllPostLinks changes. Related-ID queries repeatedly scan all links. getQueryComplementByTag uses substring LIKE and special java/javascript rule, not exact tag membership. No runtime executed.

ClassifyService fully read in bounded line ranges after initial output truncation. Active main path trains Stanford/Weka seven-feature models; only observed call to createFeaturesForSimpleClassifier here is inside commented-out getInstances. Five-slot helper defect is not on this active path; other test callers remain unread.

Train/test split selects every index with i%(100/floatPercent)==0 after reversing an unordered fetched pair list, then removes selected pairs only. It does not exclude all pairs sharing tested question IDs or duplicate families, so question/family leakage is possible. Nondivisor percentage behavior uses float modulo, not exact requested percentage; invalid values unvalidated. Balanced negative prefix assumes sufficient rows.

Query candidates include self then filter it, consuming retrieval budget. Rankings rerank same bounded pool and crop to1000; verifyHit checks first direct postlink master hit, so reported recall@k is query hit rate against direct labels, not all-pair recall or precision. Tied scores sort from HashMap without explicit tie key. No false-positive/calibration metric.

Search errors continue after count increment; final recall values are updated only on successful iterations, so trailing failed queries can leave stored rate denominators stale relative to recorded totalQuestionsToTest. Outer run catch logs and swallows failures. Experiment and five rate rows saved separately without an enclosing transaction here; default-locale DecimalFormat text reparsed as Double can fail under comma-decimal locales. No runtime or DB actions executed.

Pair,Feature,PostLink,Question models fully read. Pair equality/hash use only mutable database ID; distinct unsaved pairs with null IDs compare equal and assigning ID changes hash bucket identity. Training removeAll therefore removes selected persisted row IDs, not all shared question/family pairs. Active ranking assigns per-query retrieval index IDs, preventing ordinary distinct-index collapse but not providing cross-query semantic identity.

Feature equality uses only pairId, ignoring feature type and own ID; same-pair seven feature types compare equal under equals despite different cosine values. Current map keys by type avoid that specific collapse, but arbitrary feature sets/dedup calls would not. PostLink equality includes ordered postId/relatedPostId only, excluding relation type/date; Question equality only ID with null-ID equality. Models expose mutable nullable fields without numerical/schema invariants; no runtime validation performed.

Remaining three domain models and six CRUD repository interfaces fully read. All main Java source modules now read. Experiment/RecallRate store counts/rates/config but lack source corpus digest, random seed, held-out question list, query-error counts or completion state. Setters do not enforce finite/range/monotonic hit invariants; ID-only equality retains null-ID behavior. Post exposes mutable source text and metadata without version receipt.

FeatureRepository deletes features by selected pair tag; PairRepository then deletes selected tag rows. No uniqueness constraint for pair endpoints or pairId/type is declared in inspected model annotations; database schema still unread, so database-level constraints remain unverified. Repository interfaces add no corpus validation or transactional all-report publication contract. No database execution performed.

Schema,analysis SQL,POM,logback and tiny committed log fully read. Schema confirms no unique pair endpoints/tag or pairId/type constraint, no self-pair prohibition and no cosine/recall finite/range/monotonic checks. Feature has FK pair and report has cascading experiment FK, but no report-origin uniqueness. Numeric cosine quantized four decimals and recall two, so persisted feature values differ from full-precision newly computed query features.

POM targets Java8/SpringBoot1.5.1 with Lucene5.5.4,Terrier4.2,Stanford3.7,Weka3.8.1,Liblinear/Mallet. No explicit custom test-skipping setting in POM, but README build recipe passes maven.test.skip=true. Actual inherited lifecycle/run outcomes not executed. Three-line2017log is startup only, no completed test or metric evidence. Analysis SQL is a query plus commented manual edits, not executed.

Seven classifier demonstration files fully read. They expose main methods with printed outputs, no JUnit@Test or asserted expected predictions. Three LibLinear examples use authored tiny arrays; Test2/Test3 probability calls mistakenly pass trainingSet[i] while nearby prediction uses testSet[i], so printed probabilities do not qualify test points.

Mallet demonstration creates second positive instance from first vector despite defining vector2, then evaluates a single exact copy of a training vector. Weka likewise evaluates an exact training-vector copy; Stanford uses four synthetic records. These are API examples, not held-out accuracy/precision/recall qualification. SimpleLogistic test is a copied implementation requiring untracked dataset.txt. None executed; two larger test files remain unread.

DupeTest fully read. Class mixes extends TestCase with SpringRunner/SpringBootTest; every visible @Test annotation is commented and there are no expected-value assertions. testSearch has JUnit3-style name but actual discovery under configured runner/lifecycle not executed, so no positive test-count claim. Its single-document RAM search prints hits only; gravaResultados saves fabricated metric rows with counts exceeding10recordedqueries, not a measured validation.

Spring context startup can trigger already-read PostConstruct application flow and database writes, so merely launching this file would not be an isolated numeric regression. No Spring/Maven/DB execution performed. One remaining large Tests.java remains unread; all test/demo definitions read so far supply no asserted dedup correctness gate.

Tests.java fully read, completing all9test/demo Java source files. It is a plain main/constructor scratchpad with tokenization, substring, regex, rounding, random-number, queue and map examples; search demo prints seven-document hits without assertions. No active JUnit annotations, testcase inheritance or asserted expected results in this file. Constructor invokes GC/finalization and random samples but none was executed.

Across all inspected test sources no independently asserted file/pixel/text-dedup correctness suite exists. Demonstration code and class names are not passing tests. Tokenization pipeline stems before lowercasing in this scratchpad; not active application preprocessing. Core Java source and tests now fully read, but committed class files and residual SQL/config/license still outstanding.

Remaining query scratchpad,MIT license,packaged logback and Maven metadata fully read; two application.properties files parsed structurally with connection values withheld. Query scratchpad mixes SELECT,COPY,exports,DELETE and INSERT examples with no transaction/idempotent migration design. None executed. Numeric counts and NaN-query examples are historical comments/queries,not current database results.
